title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
text: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence. Any other criminal conspiracy is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine, or with both.

title: Unlawful assembly
text: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an 'unlawful assembly' if the common object of the persons composing it is to overawe the government, resist execution of law, commit mischief or trespass, forcibly take possession of property, or compel a person to do what he is not legally bound to do.

title: Punishment for being member of unlawful assembly
text: Whoever is a member of an unlawful assembly shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

title: Punishment for rioting
text: Whoever is guilty of rioting shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
text: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
text: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, every person who at the time of committing that offence was a member of the same assembly is guilty of that offence.

title: Promoting enmity between different groups
text: Whoever promotes disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
text: Whoever drives any vehicle on a public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

title: Punishment for murder
text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
text: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act is done with the intention of causing death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both, if the act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death.

title: Causing death by negligence
text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Dowry death
text: Where the death of a woman is caused by burns or bodily injury within seven years of marriage, and it is shown that she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry, such death is called dowry death, and the husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death and punished with imprisonment for a term not less than seven years, extendable to life imprisonment.

title: Abetment of suicide
text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Attempt to murder
text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that if he by that act caused death he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused, may be punished with imprisonment for life.

title: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt
text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which used as a weapon of offence is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any heated substance, or poison, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Punishment for wrongful restraint
text: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

title: Punishment for wrongful confinement
text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
text: A man committing physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, a demand or request for sexual favours, showing pornography against the will of a woman, or making sexually coloured remarks, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both, depending on the specific act.

title: Punishment for rape
text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Unnatural offences
text: Whoever voluntarily has carnal intercourse against the order of nature with any man, woman or animal, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. (Consensual acts between adults have been read down by the Supreme Court in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India.)

title: Punishment for theft
text: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Theft in dwelling house
text: Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel which is used as a human dwelling or for custody of property shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Robbery
text: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. Theft is robbery if, in committing the theft, the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.

title: Punishment for robbery
text: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the robbery is committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may extend to fourteen years.

title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
text: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, banker, merchant or agent
text: Whoever, being in a position of trust as a public servant, banker, merchant, or agent, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of property entrusted to him, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Cheating
text: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property, or to consent to retention of property, or intentionally induces the person to do or omit to do anything which he would not otherwise do or omit, is said to cheat.

title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Criminal trespass
text: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered, unlawfully remains there with such intent, is said to commit criminal trespass.

title: Punishment for criminal trespass
text: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

title: Punishment for house-trespass
text: Whoever commits house-trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

title: Forgery
text: Whoever makes any false document or part of a document with intent to cause damage or injury, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, commits forgery.

title: Punishment for forgery
text: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage
text: Every man who deceitfully causes any woman not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
text: Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries again in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of it taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty
text: Whoever, being the husband or relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Cruelty includes wilful conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide or grave injury, and harassment connected with unlawful demand for property or dowry.

title: Defamation
text: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing it is likely to harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person, subject to certain exceptions.

title: Punishment for defamation
text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Criminal intimidation
text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, commits criminal intimidation.

title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace
text: Whoever intentionally insults, and thereby gives provocation to any person, intending or knowing it likely that such provocation will cause him to break the public peace, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, or to an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, the imprisonment may extend to seven years.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
text: Whoever intends to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or gesture shall be seen or heard by such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.

title: When police may arrest without warrant
text: Any police officer may without an order from a magistrate and without a warrant arrest any person who commits a cognizable offence in his presence, or who is reasonably suspected of having committed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment, subject to conditions laid down in Arnesh Kumar guidelines for offences punishable with less than seven years.

title: Arrest how made
text: In making an arrest, the police officer shall actually touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless there is submission to custody by word or action. Confinement may be secured by all means necessary if the person forcibly resists.

title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
text: Every police officer arresting any person without a warrant shall forthwith communicate to him the full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested, and if the offence is bailable, shall inform him that he is entitled to be released on bail.

title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing and read over to the informant, and every such information shall be signed by the person giving it. A copy of the FIR shall be given free of cost to the informant.

title: Police officer's power to investigate cognizable case
text: Any officer in charge of a police station may, without the order of a magistrate, investigate any cognizable case which a court having jurisdiction over the local area would have power to inquire into or try.

title: Examination of witnesses by police
text: Any police officer investigating a case may examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case, and such person shall be bound to answer all questions truly, except questions the answers to which would expose him to a criminal charge.

title: Recording of confessions and statements
text: Any Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate may record any confession or statement made to him in the course of an investigation, and shall, before recording a confession, explain to the person making it that he is not bound to make the confession.

title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours
text: When a person is arrested and detained and the investigation cannot be completed within 24 hours, the officer in charge shall forward the accused to the nearest magistrate, who may authorize detention not exceeding 15 days at a time, subject to overall limits of 60 or 90 days depending on the offence, after which the accused is entitled to default bail.

title: Report of police officer on completion of investigation (chargesheet)
text: Every investigation shall be completed without unnecessary delay, and on completion the officer in charge shall forward to the magistrate a report (chargesheet) stating the names of the parties, the nature of the information, and whether an offence appears to have been committed and by whom.

title: Cognizance of offences by magistrates
text: Any magistrate may take cognizance of any offence upon receiving a complaint of facts constituting such offence, upon a police report of such facts, or upon information received from any person other than a police officer, or upon his own knowledge.

title: Prosecution of judges and public servants
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant in discharge of his official duties, except with the previous sanction of the appropriate government, in order to protect public servants from harassment for acts done in an official capacity.

title: Examination of complainant
text: A magistrate taking cognizance of an offence on complaint shall examine upon oath the complainant and the witnesses present, and reduce the substance of such examination to writing, which shall be signed by the complainant, the witnesses, and the magistrate.

title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
text: A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail by a court other than the High Court or Court of Session, unless there appear reasonable grounds to believe he has committed an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (anticipatory bail)
text: When any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or Court of Session for a direction that in the event of such arrest he shall be released on bail.

title: Right to Equality
text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This guarantees that all persons are treated alike under similar circumstances, prohibiting arbitrary discrimination by the State.

title: Prohibition of discrimination
text: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth, in respect of access to shops, public restaurants, wells, roads, and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds.

title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
text: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression, to assemble peaceably, to form associations or unions, to move freely throughout India, to reside and settle in any part of India, and to practise any profession or carry on any occupation, trade or business, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

title: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
text: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that prescribed by the law in force at the time, and no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once (double jeopardy protection).

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This has been interpreted expansively by the Supreme Court to include the right to live with dignity, privacy, health, a clean environment, and a speedy trial.

title: Right to education
text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.

title: Protection against arrest and detention
text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, and shall have the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. Every arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, excluding travel time.

title: Right to Constitutional Remedies
text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the fundamental rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. The Supreme Court has the power to issue directions, orders or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, for enforcement of fundamental rights.

title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
text: Every High Court has the power to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, to any person or authority within its territorial jurisdiction, for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

title: Right to property
text: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. This provision, while not a fundamental right after the 44th Amendment, remains a constitutional right protecting citizens against arbitrary deprivation of property by the State.

title: Culpable homicide
text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (successor provision to IPC Section 299).

title: Punishment for murder
text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (successor provision to IPC Section 302).

title: Punishment for murder by five or more persons on grounds of race, caste, etc.
text: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and with fine, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

title: Attempt to murder
text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that if he by that act caused death he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and fine, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (successor provision to IPC Section 307).

title: Organised crime
text: Whoever, as a member of an organised crime syndicate, commits an offence of organised crime including extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, or cybercrime, shall be punished under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, with imprisonment which may extend to imprisonment for life and fine.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine up to ten thousand rupees, or with both, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (successor provision to IPC Section 323).

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (successor provision to IPC Section 325).

title: Request for obtaining information
text: A person desirous of obtaining information may make a request in writing or through electronic means, in English, Hindi or the official language of the area, accompanied by prescribed fees, to the Public Information Officer specifying the particulars of the information sought, without being required to give any reason for the request.

title: Disposal of request
text: On receipt of a request, the Public Information Officer shall, as expeditiously as possible and in any case within thirty days of receipt, either provide the information on payment of prescribed fee, or reject the request; where the information concerns life or liberty of a person, it shall be provided within forty-eight hours.

title: Exemption from disclosure of information
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, there shall be no obligation to give citizens information relating to matters affecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, information forbidden by a court, or information which would impede investigation, subject to a general public interest override.

title: Appeal
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Public Information Officer, or who has not received a response within the prescribed time, may prefer an appeal to a designated senior officer within thirty days, and a second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission thereafter.

title: Penalties
text: Where the Information Commission finds that a Public Information Officer has, without reasonable cause, refused to receive an application, delayed furnishing information, or acted malafide, it may impose a penalty of two hundred and fifty rupees per day up to a maximum of twenty-five thousand rupees.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
text: This Act is called the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act No. 35 of 2019), which received assent on 9th August 2019. It extends to the whole of India (originally except the State of Jammu and Kashmir; extended to the Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh by Notification S.O. 3912(E) dated 30th October 2019). It came into force on such dates as the Central Government appointed by notification, and different dates could be appointed for different States and for different provisions, the principal provisions being brought into force on 20th July 2020 and 24th July 2020. Save as otherwise expressly provided by the Central Government by notification, the Act applies to all goods and services.

title: Definitions (overview of section 2)
text: Section 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 contains forty-seven definitions which govern the whole Act unless the context otherwise requires. The defined expressions are: advertisement, appropriate laboratory, branch office, Central Authority, complainant, complaint, consumer, consumer dispute, consumer rights, defect, deficiency, design, direct selling, Director-General, District Commission, e-commerce, electronic service provider, endorsement, establishment, express warranty, goods, harm, injury, manufacturer, mediation, mediator, member, misleading advertisement, National Commission, notification, person, prescribed, product, product liability, product liability action, product manufacturer, product seller, product service provider, regulations, Regulator, restrictive trade practice, service, spurious goods, State Commission, trader, unfair contract and unfair trade practice.

title: Definition of advertisement [section 2(1)]
text: 'Advertisement' means any audio or visual publicity, representation, endorsement or pronouncement made by means of light, sound, smoke, gas, print, electronic media, internet or website, and includes any notice, circular, label, wrapper, invoice or such other documents. In an e-commerce context, a banner on a shopping app, a product listing page, a push notification announcing a sale and the label or invoice accompanying a delivered parcel are all advertisements.

title: Definition of appropriate laboratory [section 2(2)]
text: 'Appropriate laboratory' means a laboratory or organisation recognised by the Central Government, or recognised by a State Government subject to guidelines issued by the Central Government, or established by or under any law in force which is maintained, financed or aided by the Central or a State Government for carrying out analysis or test of any goods with a view to determining whether such goods suffer from any defect. A Commission refers sealed samples of goods to such a laboratory under section 38(2)(c).

title: Definition of branch office [section 2(3)]
text: 'Branch office' means any office or place of work described as a branch by the establishment, or any establishment carrying on either the same or substantially the same activity as that carried on by the head office of the establishment. The concept matters for territorial jurisdiction, because a complaint may be instituted where the opposite party has a branch office.

title: Definition of Central Authority [section 2(4)]
text: 'Central Authority' means the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) established under section 10 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of the public and consumers, and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class.

title: Definition of complainant [section 2(5)]
text: 'Complainant' means a consumer; or any voluntary consumer association registered under any law in force; or the Central Government or any State Government; or the Central Authority; or one or more consumers where there are numerous consumers having the same interest; or, in case of death of a consumer, his legal heir or legal representative; or, in case of a consumer being a minor, his parent or legal guardian. A registered online-buyers' association can therefore complain against an e-commerce platform even where it was not itself the purchaser.

title: Definition of complaint [section 2(6)]
text: 'Complaint' means any allegation in writing, made by a complainant for obtaining any relief under the Act, that: (i) an unfair contract or unfair trade practice or a restrictive trade practice has been adopted by any trader or service provider; (ii) the goods bought or agreed to be bought suffer from one or more defects; (iii) the services hired or availed of or agreed to be hired or availed of suffer from any deficiency; (iv) a trader or service provider has charged a price in excess of the price fixed by law, displayed on the goods or package, displayed on the price list, or agreed between the parties; (v) goods hazardous to life and safety are being offered for sale to the public in contravention of safety standards, or where the trader knows the goods so offered are unsafe; (vi) services hazardous or likely to be hazardous to life and safety are offered by a person who knows them to be injurious to life and safety; (vii) a claim for product liability action lies against the product manufacturer, product seller or product service provider. For example, an online marketplace charging more than the MRP printed on the pack is a complaint under clause (iv).

title: Definition of consumer [section 2(7)]
text: 'Consumer' means any person who (i) buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, and includes any user of such goods other than the buyer when such use is made with the approval of the buyer, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose; or (ii) hires or avails of any service for such consideration, and includes any beneficiary of the service other than the person who hired it, when the service is availed of with the approval of that person, but does not include a person who avails of such service for any commercial purpose. Explanation: 'commercial purpose' does not include use by a person of goods bought and used by him exclusively for earning his livelihood by means of self-employment; and the expressions 'buys any goods' and 'hires or avails any services' include offline or online transactions through electronic means, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing. This explanation is the provision that squarely brings online shoppers on e-commerce platforms within the definition of consumer.

title: Definition of consumer dispute [section 2(8)]
text: 'Consumer dispute' means a dispute where the person against whom a complaint has been made denies or disputes the allegations contained in the complaint. Where an e-commerce seller admits a defect and refunds at once there is no consumer dispute; the dispute arises when the seller contests the allegation.

title: Definition of consumer rights [section 2(9)]
text: 'Consumer rights' includes: (i) the right to be protected against the marketing of goods, products or services which are hazardous to life and property; (ii) the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods, products or services so as to protect the consumer against unfair trade practices; (iii) the right to be assured, wherever possible, access to a variety of goods, products or services at competitive prices; (iv) the right to be heard and to be assured that consumer's interests will receive due consideration at appropriate fora; (v) the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation of consumers; and (vi) the right to consumer awareness. These six rights are the statutory core that the Central Authority is charged with protecting for consumers as a class.

title: Definition of defect [section 2(10)]
text: 'Defect' means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law in force, or under any contract, express or implied, or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods or product; and the expression 'defective' is construed accordingly. A phone delivered by an online seller with a battery capacity lower than the specification advertised on the listing suffers from a defect.

title: Definition of deficiency [section 2(11)]
text: 'Deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law in force, or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service, and includes (i) any act of negligence or omission or commission by such person which causes loss or injury to the consumer, and (ii) deliberate withholding of relevant information by such person to the consumer. Failure of an e-commerce platform to deliver within the promised delivery window, or concealment of a non-returnable condition, is a deficiency in service.

title: Definition of design [section 2(12)]
text: 'Design', in relation to a product, means the intended or known physical and material characteristics of such product and includes any intended or known formulation or content of such product and the usual result of the intended manufacturing or other process used to produce such product. This definition supports the ground of 'defective in design' in a product liability action under section 84(1)(b).

title: Definition of direct selling [section 2(13)]
text: 'Direct selling' means marketing, distribution and sale of goods or provision of services through a network of sellers, other than through a permanent retail location. Section 94 empowers the Central Government to prescribe measures to prevent unfair trade practices in direct selling as well as e-commerce.

title: Definition of Director-General [section 2(14)]
text: 'Director-General' means the Director-General appointed under sub-section (2) of section 15, who heads the Investigation Wing of the Central Consumer Protection Authority and conducts inquiries or investigations as directed by the Central Authority.

title: Definition of District Commission [section 2(15)]
text: 'District Commission' means a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission established under sub-section (1) of section 28. It is the entry-level adjudicatory forum for consumer complaints.

title: Definition of e-commerce [section 2(16)]
text: 'E-commerce' means buying or selling of goods or services including digital products over digital or electronic network. This definition, read with the Explanation to section 2(7) and with section 94, is the foundation of the 2019 Act's express regulation of online marketplaces and inventory-model online sellers.

title: Definition of electronic service provider [section 2(17)]
text: 'Electronic service provider' means a person who provides technologies or processes to enable a product seller to engage in advertising or selling goods or services to a consumer and includes any online market place or online auction sites. An electronic service provider can be directed under section 38(4) to furnish information, documents or records, and can be served notice under section 65(2) at the address provided on its electronic platform through its designated nodal officer.

title: Definition of endorsement [section 2(18)]
text: 'Endorsement', in relation to an advertisement, means (i) any message, verbal statement or demonstration; or (ii) depiction of the name, signature, likeness or other identifiable personal characteristics of an individual; or (iii) depiction of the name or seal of any institution or organisation, which makes the consumer believe that it reflects the opinion, finding or experience of the person making such endorsement. Endorsers of false or misleading advertisements face penalties and endorsement bans under section 21.

title: Definition of establishment [section 2(19)]
text: 'Establishment' includes an advertising agency, commission agent, manufacturing, trading or any other commercial agency which carries on any business, trade or profession or any work in connection with or incidental or ancillary to any commercial activity, trade or profession, or such other class or classes of persons including public utility entities in the manner as may be prescribed.

title: Definition of express warranty [section 2(20)]
text: 'Express warranty' means any material statement, affirmation of fact, promise or description relating to a product or service warranting that it conforms to such material statement, affirmation, promise or description, and includes any sample or model of a product warranting that the whole of such product conforms to such sample or model. Non-conformity to an express warranty is a ground of liability of a product manufacturer under section 84(1)(d) and of a product service provider under section 85(d).

title: Definition of goods [section 2(21)]
text: 'Goods' means every kind of movable property and includes 'food' as defined in clause (j) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Groceries and packaged food ordered through an online grocery platform are therefore goods for the purposes of this Act.

title: Definition of harm [section 2(22)]
text: 'Harm', in relation to a product liability, includes (i) damage to any property other than the product itself; (ii) personal injury, illness or death; (iii) mental agony or emotional distress attendant to personal injury or illness or damage to property; or (iv) any loss of consortium or services or other loss resulting from such harm. It does not include any harm caused to a product itself, or damage to property on account of breach of warranty conditions, or any commercial or economic loss, including any direct, incidental or consequential loss relating thereto.

title: Definition of injury [section 2(23)]
text: 'Injury' means any harm whatever illegally caused to any person, in body, mind or property.

title: Definition of manufacturer [section 2(24)]
text: 'Manufacturer' means a person who (i) makes any goods or parts thereof; or (ii) assembles any goods or parts thereof made by others; or (iii) puts or causes to be put his own mark on any goods made by any other person. A private-label brand of an online retailer that applies its own mark to goods made by a third-party factory is a manufacturer.

title: Definition of mediation [section 2(25)]
text: 'Mediation' means the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes. Chapter V of the Act establishes mediation as a statutory alternative dispute resolution mechanism for consumer disputes.

title: Definition of mediator [section 2(26)]
text: 'Mediator' means a mediator referred to in section 75, that is, a person on the panel of mediators prepared by the National, State or District Commission and maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it.

title: Definition of member [section 2(27)]
text: 'Member' includes the President and a member of the National Commission or a State Commission or a District Commission, as the case may be.

title: Definition of misleading advertisement [section 2(28)]
text: 'Misleading advertisement', in relation to any product or service, means an advertisement which (i) falsely describes such product or service; or (ii) gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service; or (iii) conveys an express or implied representation which, if made by the manufacturer or seller or service provider, would constitute an unfair trade practice; or (iv) deliberately conceals important information. A listing on a shopping app that omits the fact that the price excludes a mandatory installation charge deliberately conceals important information.

title: Definition of National Commission [section 2(29)]
text: 'National Commission' means the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission established under sub-section (1) of section 53.

title: Definition of notification [section 2(30)]
text: 'Notification' means a notification published in the Official Gazette and the term 'notify' shall be construed accordingly.

title: Definition of person [section 2(31)]
text: 'Person' includes (i) an individual; (ii) a firm whether registered or not; (iii) a Hindu undivided family; (iv) a co-operative society; (v) an association of persons whether registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or not; (vi) any corporation, company or a body of individuals whether incorporated or not; and (vii) any artificial juridical person not falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses.

title: Definition of prescribed [section 2(32)]
text: 'Prescribed' means prescribed by rules made by the Central Government or, as the case may be, the State Government, under sections 101 and 102 respectively.

title: Definition of product [section 2(33)]
text: 'Product' means any article or goods or substance or raw material or any extended cycle of such product, which may be in gaseous, liquid, or solid state possessing intrinsic value which is capable of delivery either as wholly assembled or as a component part and is produced for introduction to trade or commerce, but does not include human tissues, blood, blood products and organs.

title: Definition of product liability [section 2(34)]
text: 'Product liability' means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto. Chapter VI (sections 82 to 87) gives effect to this concept, which was newly introduced by the 2019 Act.

title: Definition of product liability action [section 2(35)]
text: 'Product liability action' means a complaint filed by a person before a District Commission or State Commission or National Commission, as the case may be, for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him.

title: Definition of product manufacturer [section 2(36)]
text: 'Product manufacturer' means a person who (i) makes any product or parts thereof; or (ii) assembles parts thereof made by others; or (iii) puts or causes to be put his own mark on any products made by any other person; or (iv) makes a product and sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains such product or is otherwise involved in placing such product for commercial purpose; or (v) designs, produces, fabricates, constructs or re-manufactures any product before its sale; or (vi) being a product seller of a product, is also a manufacturer of such product.

title: Definition of product seller [section 2(37)]
text: 'Product seller', in relation to a product, means a person who, in the course of business, imports, sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains, or is otherwise involved in placing such product for commercial purpose, and includes a manufacturer who is also a product seller, and a service provider. It does not include (a) a seller of immovable property, unless engaged in the sale of a constructed house or the construction of homes or flats; (b) a provider of professional services in any transaction in which the sale or use of a product is only incidental, the essence of the transaction being the furnishing of opinion, skill or services; or (c) a person who acts only in a financial capacity with respect to the sale of the product, or is not a manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor, retailer, direct seller or an electronic service provider, or leases a product without having a reasonable opportunity to inspect and discover defects under a lease arrangement in which selection, possession, maintenance and operation of the product are controlled by a person other than the lessor.

title: Definition of product service provider [section 2(38)]
text: 'Product service provider', in relation to a product, means a person who provides any service in respect of such product. An authorised service centre that repairs an appliance bought online is a product service provider and is liable under section 85 on the grounds stated there.

title: Definition of regulations [section 2(39)]
text: 'Regulations' means the regulations made by the National Commission, or as the case may be, the Central Authority, under sections 103 and 104 respectively.

title: Definition of Regulator [section 2(40)]
text: 'Regulator' means a body or any authority established under any other law for the time being in force. Under section 19(2), the Central Authority may, after preliminary inquiry, refer a matter to the concerned sectoral Regulator along with its report.

title: Definition of restrictive trade practice [section 2(41)]
text: 'Restrictive trade practice' means a trade practice which tends to bring about manipulation of price or its conditions of delivery or to affect flow of supplies in the market relating to goods or services in such a manner as to impose on the consumers unjustified costs or restrictions and shall include (i) delay beyond the period agreed to by a trader in supply of such goods or in providing the services which has led or is likely to lead to rise in the price; and (ii) any trade practice which requires a consumer to buy, hire or avail of any goods or services as a condition precedent for buying, hiring or availing of other goods or services. Compulsory bundling of an extended warranty with an online electronics purchase is an example of clause (ii).

title: Definition of service [section 2(42)]
text: 'Service' means service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes, but is not limited to, the provision of facilities in connection with banking, financing, insurance, transport, processing, supply of electrical or other energy, telecom, boarding or lodging or both, housing construction, entertainment, amusement or the purveying of news or other information, but does not include the rendering of any service free of charge or under a contract of personal service. Note that telecom and housing construction are expressly named in the 2019 Act, unlike the 1986 Act.

title: Definition of spurious goods [section 2(43)]
text: 'Spurious goods' means such goods which are falsely claimed to be genuine. Manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing or importing spurious goods is punishable under section 91.

title: Definition of State Commission [section 2(44)]
text: 'State Commission' means a State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission established under sub-section (1) of section 42.

title: Definition of trader [section 2(45)]
text: 'Trader', in relation to any goods, means a person who sells or distributes any goods for sale and includes the manufacturer thereof, and where such goods are sold or distributed in package form, includes the packer thereof.

title: Definition of unfair contract [section 2(46)]
text: 'Unfair contract' means a contract between a manufacturer or trader or service provider on one hand, and a consumer on the other, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, namely: (i) requiring manifestly excessive security deposits to be given by a consumer for the performance of contractual obligations; (ii) imposing any penalty on the consumer for the breach of contract which is wholly disproportionate to the loss occurred due to such breach to the other party to the contract; (iii) refusing to accept early repayment of debts on payment of applicable penalty; (iv) entitling a party to the contract to terminate such contract unilaterally, without reasonable cause; (v) permitting or has the effect of permitting one party to assign the contract to the detriment of the other party who is a consumer, without his consent; or (vi) imposing on the consumer any unreasonable charge, obligation or condition which puts such consumer to disadvantage. A clause in an e-commerce platform's terms allowing it to cancel a confirmed order unilaterally without cause falls within clause (iv). Unfair contract complaints are separately dealt with in the jurisdiction provisions of sections 47 and 58, and a State or National Commission may declare such terms null and void under sections 49(2) and 59(2).

title: Definition of unfair trade practice [section 2(47)]
text: 'Unfair trade practice' means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice, including: (i) making any statement, whether orally or in writing or by visible representation including by means of electronic record, which falsely represents that goods are of a particular standard, quality, quantity, grade, composition, style or model; falsely represents that services are of a particular standard, quality or grade; falsely represents re-built, second-hand, renovated, reconditioned or old goods as new; represents that goods or services have sponsorship, approval, performance, characteristics, accessories, uses or benefits which they do not have; represents that the seller or supplier has a sponsorship, approval or affiliation which he does not have; makes a false or misleading representation concerning the need for, or usefulness of, any goods or services; gives a warranty or guarantee of performance, efficacy or length of life not based on adequate or proper test (the burden of proving an adequate test lies on the person raising that defence); makes a representation purporting to be a warranty or guarantee, or a promise to replace, maintain or repair until a specified result is achieved, where it is materially misleading or there is no reasonable prospect of it being carried out; materially misleads the public concerning the price at which such products or like products have been or are ordinarily sold; or gives false or misleading facts disparaging the goods, services or trade of another person; (ii) permitting the publication of any bargain-price advertisement for goods or services not intended to be offered at that bargain price, or for a period and in quantities that are not reasonable; (iii) permitting the offering of gifts, prizes or other items with the intention of not providing them as offered, or creating the impression that something is being given free when it is wholly or partly covered by the amount charged; the conduct of any contest, lottery, game of chance or skill for promoting the sale, use or supply of any product or business interest (except as may be prescribed); or withholding from participants of a prize scheme, on its closure, the information about the final results; (iv) permitting the sale or supply of goods knowing or having reason to believe that the goods do not comply with standards prescribed by the competent authority relating to performance, composition, contents, design, constructions, finishing or packaging as are necessary to prevent or reduce the risk of injury to the person using the goods; (v) permitting the hoarding or destruction of goods, or refusal to sell the goods or to make them available for sale or to provide any service, if such conduct raises or tends to raise or is intended to raise the cost of those or other similar goods or services; (vi) manufacturing of spurious goods or offering such goods for sale or adopting deceptive practices in the provision of services; (vii) not issuing bill or cash memo or receipt for the goods sold or services rendered in such manner as may be prescribed; (viii) refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or, in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days; and (ix) disclosing to other person any personal information given in confidence by the consumer unless such disclosure is made in accordance with the provisions of any law in force. Clauses (viii) and (ix) are new in the 2019 Act and directly address e-commerce grievances such as refusal to honour a return within thirty days and leakage of customer data by an online seller.

title: Central Consumer Protection Council
text: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish the Central Consumer Protection Council, known as the Central Council. It shall be an advisory council consisting of the Minister-in-charge of the Department of Consumer Affairs in the Central Government as Chairperson, and such number of other official or non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed.

title: Procedure for meetings of Central Council
text: The Central Council shall meet as and when necessary, but at least one meeting of the Council shall be held every year. It shall meet at such time and place as the Chairperson may think fit and shall observe such procedure in regard to the transaction of its business as may be prescribed.

title: Objects of Central Council
text: The objects of the Central Council shall be to render advice on promotion and protection of the consumers' rights under this Act.

title: State Consumer Protection Councils
text: Every State Government shall, by notification, establish a State Consumer Protection Council for that State, known as the State Council. It is an advisory council consisting of the Minister-in-charge of Consumer Affairs in the State Government as Chairperson, such number of other official or non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed, and such number of other official or non-official members, not exceeding ten, as may be nominated by the Central Government. The State Council shall meet as and when necessary but not less than two meetings shall be held every year, at such time and place as the Chairperson thinks fit and following such procedure as may be prescribed.

title: Objects of State Council
text: The objects of every State Council shall be to render advice on promotion and protection of consumer rights under this Act within the State.

title: District Consumer Protection Council
text: The State Government shall, by notification, establish for every District a District Consumer Protection Council, known as the District Council. It is an advisory council consisting of the Collector of the district (by whatever name called) as Chairperson and such number of other official and non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed. The District Council shall meet as and when necessary but not less than two meetings shall be held every year, at such time and place within the district as the Chairperson thinks fit and following such procedure as may be prescribed.

title: Objects of District Council
text: The objects of every District Council shall be to render advice on promotion and protection of consumer rights under this Act within the district.

title: Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority
text: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a Central Consumer Protection Authority, known as the Central Authority, to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers, and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class. The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, appointed by the Central Government. Its headquarters shall be at such place in the National Capital Region of Delhi as the Central Government decides, and it shall have regional and other offices at any other place in India as the Central Government may decide.

title: Qualifications, method of recruitment, etc., of Chief Commissioner and Commissioners
text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for the qualifications for appointment, method of recruitment, procedure for appointment, term of office, salaries and allowances, resignation, removal and other terms and conditions of service of the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners of the Central Authority.

title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Central Authority
text: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.

title: Appointment of officers, experts, professionals and other employees of Central Authority
text: The Central Government shall provide the Central Authority such number of officers and other employees as it considers necessary for the efficient performance of its functions, on such salaries, allowances and terms and conditions of service as may be prescribed. The Central Authority may also engage, in accordance with the procedure specified by regulations, such number of experts and professionals of integrity and ability having special knowledge and experience in the areas of consumer rights and welfare, consumer policy, law, medicine, food safety, health, engineering, product safety, commerce, economics, public affairs or administration as it deems necessary to assist it.

title: Procedure of Central Authority
text: The Central Authority shall regulate the procedure for transaction of its business and allocation of its business amongst the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners as may be specified by regulations. The Chief Commissioner shall have the powers of general superintendence, direction and control in respect of all administrative matters of the Central Authority, and may delegate such of his powers relating to administrative matters as he thinks fit to any Commissioner (including a Commissioner of a regional office) or any other officer of the Central Authority.

title: Investigation Wing
text: The Central Authority shall have an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General for the purpose of conducting inquiry or investigation under this Act as may be directed by the Central Authority. The Central Government may appoint a Director-General and such number of Additional Director-General, Director, Joint Director, Deputy Director and Assistant Director from among persons who have experience in investigation and possess such qualifications, in such manner, as may be prescribed. Every such officer shall exercise his powers and discharge his functions subject to the general control, supervision and direction of the Director-General, who may delegate all or any of his powers to them while conducting inquiries or investigations. The inquiries or investigations made by the Director-General shall be submitted to the Central Authority in such form, manner and within such time as may be specified by regulations.

title: Power of District Collector
text: The District Collector (by whatever name called) may, on a complaint or on a reference made to him by the Central Authority or the Commissioner of a regional office, inquire into or investigate complaints regarding violation of rights of consumers as a class, on matters relating to violations of consumer rights, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements, within his jurisdiction, and submit his report to the Central Authority or to the Commissioner of a regional office, as the case may be.

title: Complaints to authorities
text: A complaint relating to violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practices or false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of consumers as a class, may be forwarded either in writing or in electronic mode to any one of the authorities, namely, the District Collector, or the Commissioner of regional office, or the Central Authority.

title: Powers and functions of Central Authority
text: The Central Authority shall protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class and prevent violation of consumer rights under this Act; prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no person engages himself in unfair trade practices; ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made of any goods or services contravening this Act or the rules or regulations; and ensure that no person takes part in the publication of any advertisement which is false or misleading. For these purposes the Central Authority may: (a) inquire or cause an inquiry or investigation to be made into violations of consumer rights or unfair trade practices, either suo motu or on a complaint received or on the directions from the Central Government; (b) file complaints before the District, State or National Commission; (c) intervene in any proceedings before those Commissions in respect of any allegation of violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practices; (d) review the matters relating to, and the factors inhibiting enjoyment of, consumer rights, including safeguards provided under any other law, and recommend appropriate remedial measures; (e) recommend adoption of international covenants and best international practices on consumer rights; (f) undertake and promote research in the field of consumer rights; (g) spread and promote awareness on consumer rights; (h) encourage non-Governmental organisations and other institutions working in the field of consumer rights to co-operate with consumer protection agencies; (i) mandate the use of unique and universal goods identifiers in such goods as may be necessary to prevent unfair trade practices and protect consumers' interest; (j) issue safety notices to alert consumers against dangerous or hazardous or unsafe goods or services; (k) advise the Ministries and Departments of the Central and State Governments on consumer welfare measures; and (l) issue necessary guidelines to prevent unfair trade practices and protect consumers' interest.

title: Power of Central Authority to refer matter for investigation or to other Regulator
text: The Central Authority may, after receiving any information or complaint or directions from the Central Government or of its own motion, conduct or cause to be conducted a preliminary inquiry as to whether there exists a prima facie case of violation of consumer rights or any unfair trade practice or any false or misleading advertisement, by any person, which is prejudicial to the public interest or to the interests of consumers; and if satisfied that a prima facie case exists, it shall cause investigation to be made by the Director-General or by the District Collector. Where, after preliminary inquiry, the Central Authority is of the opinion that the matter is to be dealt with by a Regulator established under any other law, it may refer such matter to the concerned Regulator along with its report. For the purposes of investigation, the Central Authority, the Director General or the District Collector may call upon the person concerned and also direct him to produce any document or record in his possession.

title: Power of Central Authority to recall goods, etc.
text: Where the Central Authority is satisfied on the basis of investigation that there is sufficient evidence to show violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practice by a person, it may pass such order as may be necessary, including (a) recalling of goods or withdrawal of services which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe; (b) reimbursement of the prices of goods or services so recalled to purchasers of such goods or services; and (c) discontinuation of practices which are unfair and prejudicial to consumers' interest. The Central Authority shall give the person an opportunity of being heard before passing an order under this section.

title: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements
text: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after investigation that any advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer or is in contravention of consumer rights, it may by order direct the concerned trader, manufacturer, endorser, advertiser or publisher to discontinue such advertisement or to modify it in such manner and within such time as specified. It may also impose on a manufacturer or an endorser a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees, and for every subsequent contravention a penalty which may extend to fifty lakh rupees. Where it deems necessary, it may prohibit the endorser of a false or misleading advertisement from making endorsement of any product or service for a period up to one year, and for every subsequent contravention up to three years. Where any person is found to publish, or is a party to the publication of, a misleading advertisement, a penalty up to ten lakh rupees may be imposed on him. No endorser shall be liable to penalty if he has exercised due diligence to verify the veracity of the claims made in the advertisement; and no person shall be liable if he proves that he published or arranged for the publication of the advertisement in the ordinary course of his business, unless he had previous knowledge of the order passed by the Central Authority for withdrawal or modification of the advertisement. While determining the penalty, regard shall be had to the population and area impacted or affected, the frequency and duration of the offence, the vulnerability of the class of persons likely to be adversely affected, and the gross revenue from the sales effected by virtue of such offence. An opportunity of being heard must be given before any order under this section is passed.

title: Search and seizure
text: For the purpose of conducting an investigation after preliminary inquiry under section 19(1), the Director-General or any other officer authorised by him, or the District Collector, may, if he has any reason to believe that any person has violated any consumer rights or committed unfair trade practice or causes any false or misleading advertisement to be made, enter at any reasonable time into any such premises and search for and seize any document, record, article or other form of evidence; make a note or an inventory of such record or article; or require any person to produce any record, register or other document or article. The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to search and seizure shall apply as far as may be. Every document, record or article seized or produced shall be returned to the person from whom it was seized or who produced it within twenty days of the date of seizure or production, after copies or extracts certified by that person have been taken in such manner as may be prescribed. Where any seized article is subject to speedy or natural decay, the Director-General or such other officer may dispose of the article in such manner as may be prescribed; and in the case of other articles, the provisions of section 38(2)(c) apply mutatis mutandis in relation to analysis or tests.

title: Designation of any statutory authority or body to function as Central Authority
text: The Central Government may, if it considers necessary, by notification, designate any statutory authority or body to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Central Authority referred to in section 10.

title: Appeal against orders of Central Authority
text: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.

title: Grants by Central Government
text: The Central Government may, after due appropriation made by Parliament by law in this behalf, make to the Central Authority grants of such sums of money as that Government may think fit for being utilised for the purposes of this Act.

title: Accounts and audit of Central Authority
text: The Central Authority shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts in such form and manner as may be prescribed in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Its accounts shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General at such intervals as he may specify, and the expenditure of such audit shall be payable by the Central Authority to him. The Comptroller and Auditor-General or any person appointed by him shall have the same rights, privileges and authority in connection with the audit as he generally has in connection with Government accounts, including the right to demand production of books, accounts, connected vouchers and other documents and papers, and to inspect any of the offices of the Central Authority. The certified accounts together with the audit report shall be forwarded annually to the Central Government, which shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

title: Furnishing of annual reports, etc.
text: The Central Authority shall prepare once every year, in such form, manner and at such time as may be prescribed, an annual report giving a full account of its activities during the previous year and such other reports and returns as may be directed, and forward copies to the Central Government. A copy of the annual report shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is received, before each House of Parliament.

title: Establishment of District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
text: The State Government shall, by notification, establish a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, known as the District Commission, in each district of the State; and it may, if it deems fit, establish more than one District Commission in a district. Each District Commission shall consist of a President and not less than two and not more than such number of members as may be prescribed, in consultation with the Central Government.

title: Qualifications, etc., of President and members of District Commission
text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for the qualifications, method of recruitment, procedure for appointment, term of office, resignation and removal of the President and members of the District Commission.

title: Salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of service of President and members of District Commission
text: The State Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for salaries and allowances and other terms and conditions of service of the President and members of the District Commission.

title: Transitional provision for District Commission
text: Any person appointed as President or as a member of the District Commission immediately before the commencement of this Act shall hold office as such President or member till the completion of the term for which he has been appointed.

title: Vacancy in office of member of District Commission
text: If at any time there is a vacancy in the office of the President or member of a District Commission, the State Government may, by notification, direct that any other District Commission specified in that notification shall exercise the jurisdiction in respect of that district also, or that the President or a member of any other District Commission specified in the notification shall exercise the powers and discharge the functions of the President or member of that District Commission also.

title: Officers and other employees of District Commission
text: The State Government shall provide the District Commission with such officers and other employees as may be required to assist it in the discharge of its functions. Such officers and employees shall discharge their functions under the general superintendence of the President of the District Commission, and their salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of service shall be such as may be prescribed.

title: Jurisdiction of District Commission
text: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed one crore rupees, provided that where the Central Government deems it necessary it may prescribe such other value as it deems fit. A complaint shall be instituted in a District Commission within the local limits of whose jurisdiction (a) the opposite party or each of the opposite parties, where there are more than one, at the time of institution of the complaint, ordinarily resides or carries on business or has a branch office or personally works for gain; or (b) any of the opposite parties, where there are more than one, at the time of institution of the complaint, actually and voluntarily resides, or carries on business or has a branch office, or personally works for gain, provided that in such case the permission of the District Commission is given; or (c) the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises; or (d) the complainant resides or personally works for gain. Clause (d) is the significant consumer-friendly change of the 2019 Act: an online buyer can sue at his own place of residence. The District Commission shall ordinarily function in the district headquarters and may perform its functions at such other place in the district as the State Government may, in consultation with the State Commission, notify in the Official Gazette.

title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
text: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by (a) the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided, or who alleges unfair trade practice in respect of such goods or service; (b) any recognised consumer association, whether the consumer is a member of such association or not; (c) one or more consumers, where there are numerous consumers having the same interest, with the permission of the District Commission, on behalf of or for the benefit of all consumers so interested; or (d) the Central Government, the Central Authority or the State Government. Such a complaint may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed. 'Recognised consumer association' means any voluntary consumer association registered under any law in force. Every complaint shall be accompanied with such fee and payable in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed.

title: Proceedings before District Commission
text: Every proceeding before the District Commission shall be conducted by the President of that Commission and at least one member thereof, sitting together; and where a member is, for any reason, unable to conduct a proceeding till it is completed, the President and the other member shall continue the proceeding from the stage at which it was last heard by the previous member. On receipt of a complaint made under section 35, the District Commission may, by order, admit the complaint for being proceeded with or reject the same; but a complaint shall not be rejected unless an opportunity of being heard has been given to the complainant. The admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed, and where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility within that period, the complaint shall be deemed to have been admitted.

title: Reference to mediation
text: At the first hearing of the complaint after its admission, or at any later stage, if it appears to the District Commission that there exists elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, except in such cases as may be prescribed, it may direct the parties to give in writing, within five days, consent to have their dispute settled by mediation in accordance with Chapter V. Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and the provisions of Chapter V relating to mediation shall apply.

title: Procedure on admission of complaint
text: On admission of a complaint, or in respect of cases referred for mediation on failure of settlement by mediation, the District Commission shall proceed with the complaint.
